subtitle: Pull the strings of an undead cowboy

body: The Gunstringer is Twisted Pixel's Xbox 360 Kinect shooting game, first released in North America on 13 September 2011. An undead marionette sheriff rises to take revenge on the gang that betrayed him, with the story presented as a theatrical performance. The player uses hand movements rather than a gamepad: one hand guides the puppet while the other aims its gun. Live-action footage of an audience frames the adventure as a show, making the person in front of the television both performer and puppeteer within the same comic Western.

The aiming hand can select several enemies before a firing gesture sends the Gunstringer's shots towards them. Movement of the other hand guides the character through the action, translating the image of a suspended puppet into the control scheme. Some sections follow a fixed route and allow both hands to operate guns. The player therefore alternates between directing the figure and concentrating on the targets ahead. Kinect's body tracking becomes useful because the fiction explains the gesture: the hand is not pretending to hold a conventional controller but manipulating a character on a stage.

The project began as an Xbox Live Arcade game before being expanded into a full retail release. Its four acts follow different members of the former gang through exaggerated Western settings, mixing stage scenery with modern and supernatural jokes. Edward Kuehnel wrote the story for a game whose presentation makes room for both the puppet and the audience watching it. The Gunstringer became one of Kinect's more distinctive experiments by giving the input a clear theatrical purpose. The player's moving hands belong naturally to a story about a marionette finding its way across the stage.
